bugs: Back on a mix page, the X on New mix, Leave and Delete call openPlayFAM -> setTab, so each 'back' plays the tab nudge from the right instead of the pop.
Back on Add topics calls openMix -> navigate('mixdetail'): a second mix page is pushed from the right and the stack grows by one each time.
Rename, Public/Private, Make public and share, Make it yours alone re-run openMix: page pushed onto itself, /open re-sent, recs refetched, Shuffle reset.
A typed topic (id q:...) cannot be removed from a mix on the web: Add topics' tick is the only remove, and it lists catalogue topics only.
moveMixTopic draws the new order before saving and saveMix gets no failed callback, so a refused reorder stays on screen.
The CSS comment above .mix-switch says the switch means private; renderMixBody's comment and code say on = Public.
Delete mix in the ⋯ menu deletes with one tap: no confirmation and no Undo.
Opening a dormant mix writes its episodes (§359) but the open page never refreshes: rows keep topic names and the card has no READY until the next visit.
A typed topic added on Add topics appears nowhere on that screen; only the bottom line says it went in.
Mix cards are role=button divs that open on Enter but not on Space.
Dead CSS nothing in index.html draws: .focus-all, .fol-wrap, .focus-panel, .focus-bar, .pk-chip, .mix-sig-*, .mix-pill, .mix-chev, .mix-new.

animations.title: The mix glide between episodes
animations.trigger: Play on a mix, or the mix moving on to its next episode
animations.now: Overlay pops in; track slides 450ms after 100ms, (.3,1.1,.4,1); lit card 1→1.08 and dot width 6→18px, 400ms at 250ms; a cached episode cuts it at 450ms; overlay pops out.
animations.verdict: Keep the owner's glide, but land it inside the 450 ms a cached episode is shown, move the dot by transform, drop the overshoot, and fade the overlay in and out.
animations.notes: The owner's pick (§509, option 3 'Rail Glide'; cards are the episodes' pictures over the topic names since §591). paintLoadingVariant('glide') draws it into #famLoadingAlt; generate() shows #famLoading in one frame (8399) and clearGenOverlay removes it in one frame (7326). It holds nothing: genStepsGate starts audio at once (free), and finishGenOverlay keeps the screen up GEN_MIN_VISIBLE_MS = 450 ms after audio starts. Mix episodes are written at 05:00 and voiced ahead (§610), so often it is a cache hit and about 450 ms on screen. Today's timeline overruns that: track 100 ms delay + 450 ms = 550 ms; lit card and dot 250 + 400 = 650 ms, cut about half way - the pose the owner chose is never seen landing. famGlideDot animates width (layout, main thread) at the busiest moment in the app, the failure §288 fixed for the chevrons. Overshoot: famGlidePick peaks ~3% past, famGlide ~0.2% - bounce in product UI. Title: famLdUp, bare 300 ms ease. First episode: the overlay covers the mix page and, on a fast cache hit, the player push (320 ms) runs mostly beneath it, so the listener sees overlay, cut, player; a 150 ms exit fade bridges that and holds nothing (audio is already playing). Keyframes are acceptable here (a one-shot loader nothing toggles), but every option must look right if cut at any frame (skip, X, a cache hit). Staging: one lead at a time - track first, then the lit card; the title arrives with the overlay in one piece. Reduced motion today: track at --to and dot at 18 px, but the lit card stays at 1 (end state differs) and the status dot stops, though it is the one 'still working' sign; the skill keeps work indicators moving. All options: overlay instant and status dot pulsing under reduced motion. Keep LOADING_GLIDE_STEP 138, card 128 px, --from = --to + 138 (+80 on the first). The 'n of N' kicker and Played/Skipped stamps are unchanged. Origins: the lit card and the dot pill scale from their centres.

animations.title: Mix cards arriving in the grid
animations.trigger: /api/mixes lands: first visit, a new mix, a removed one
animations.now: The whole grid appears in one frame when the mixes land, often during the tab slide; a mix just made is simply there on return, a deleted one simply gone.
animations.verdict: Content arriving on its own: give it the owner's rail entrance, only for mixes not shown before so a revisit never replays; a deleted card leaves like a removed row.
animations.notes: openPlayFAM runs setTab('playfam') (content out 110 ms, in 200 ms after 90 ms) and loadMixes() in the same tick; renderMixList replaces #mixList.innerHTML when /api/mixes and the topic bank answer, typically 100-500 ms later - so on a first visit the cards pop in mid-slide or just after. On later visits the last render shows first and is replaced (same or changed). saveMix also re-renders after every edit, off screen. Rails solved this (§292): Motion.arriveRails animates only ids not drawn before (feedTopicsShown). Do the same keyed on mix id - but key on 'seen', not 'rendered': a mix made on New mix is rendered while the listener is on its page and first seen on return. Start only once the screen is no longer .arriving (Stagger: never inside a moving container); if the slide is still running, wait for it. Copies of one element: 30-50 ms apart, first 6 - the rail pick uses 40 ms and the first three per rail; here the first four (two rows). Deleted, left or un-added mixes: today the card is just gone. The owner's §298 'removing from a list' (slide out 180 ms, gap closes 200 ms) adapted to a two-column grid: an inert copy fades with an 8 px nudge, then later cards FLIP into place (straight moves). With Undo on delete (findings) the card leaves at once and comes back the same way. Guests: the locked note and the sample card (loadSampleMix) arrive likewise. Interrupt: a second render mid-entrance must not restart it (keyed). Reduced motion: everything at once.

animations.now: Each tab draws its own underline, so it jumps in one frame; the Create pill row hides (page jumps 42 px); panels swap and scroll resets - all at once.
animations.verdict: Tabs are frequent: swap the panels at once, but let one underline slide to the chosen side so the eye follows it; label colours over 150 ms.
animations.notes: showPlayfamTab toggles .on on #pfTabMixes / #pfTabCats (border-bottom-color copper on each), hides #newMixRow (32 px pill + 10 px margin), shows #catChips, swaps #mixesPane for #catHome (or #catPanel), and sets the shared scroller to the top. openPlayFAM calls showPlayfamTab('mixes') on every arrival - that call must not animate (nothing at rest plays an entrance). Build: one indicator (.pf-tabs::after: 50% wide, 2.5 px, copper, bottom -1 px) moved by transform translateX(0%) / translateX(100%) on a CSS transition, so a quick second tap turns it round from where it is (Interruptible); remove the per-tab border. Labels: colour 150 ms ease (the colour rule). The tablist has no arrow-key handling; add it, and keep keyboard switches instant. Panels: frequency says no transition (A, C). B shows the owner's app-tab nudge (§292) at page scale for comparison; it needs the Create row to keep its height (visibility hidden) or the nudge rides a 42 px jump. In A the jump is masked because the whole panel changes at once. Tenth use: 240 ms on a thin bar never delays anything - the panel is already there. Reduced motion: the underline moves in one frame.

animations.title: Category chips filtering in place
animations.trigger: tap a category row or chip, a sub-chip, or the X
animations.now: The chip row is rewritten at once (X, the category, its subs); the list becomes 'Loading today's episodes…' then the episodes, each in one frame - the line flashes on a fast answer.
animations.verdict: A many-times tap: keep it instant, but stop the flash - hold the old list until the new one lands, and say 'Loading' only past 300 ms.
animations.notes: pickCategory resets catPage, shows #catPanel in place of #catHome, rewrites the chip row (renderCategoryChips: one innerHTML), scrolls to the top and calls loadCategoryEpisodes, which writes 'Loading today’s episodes…' into #catPanel at once and the hero plus rows when /api/categories/episodes answers. pickCategorySub and the X do the same. On a quick server the loading line is up 50-200 ms: a spinner that flashes (Doherty: nothing under 300 ms, then held 500 ms). Chips are the filter of a browse page - many taps a session - so content motion is off; colour may ease (100-150 ms). A: leave the previous content in place (aria-busy), dim it to .5 only if the answer is still out at 300 ms, swap at once when it lands; the loading line only after 300 ms, held 500 ms. B, for comparison: the tapped chip is the same element before and after (FLIP from its old x to its new one), answering 'where did my chip go' when the row becomes X + category + subs. C keeps the row instant and cross-fades the panel, reusing the owner's blur-up (Motion.picture works on any background-image) for the hero. Interrupt: a second chip before the first answers already wins (catReq). Also see findings: the Categories home shows every category twice (chips and rows); category plays flash search's five steps. Reduced motion: all instant; the dim applies at once.

Don't redraw the list on success - it would kill the swap mid-flight; update the row. The glyphs are text '+' and a tick today: A stacks both in one grid cell (the icon-swap recipe without Motion: both present, classes swap, ~300 ms cubic-bezier(.25,.1,0,1), so a second tap reverses from where it is). animations.title: The deck changes when today does
animations.trigger: mixes land and a card's order, READY tag or headline changed
animations.now: The old cards stay until /api/mixes lands, then the stack, READY tag and headline change in one frame; the story just heard simply vanishes from the top.
animations.verdict: The reorder is the deck's point (§616): let the heard card go to the back and the new lead rise, as real cards would. A few times a day, so a short choreography is allowed.
animations.notes: Today's order (§616, mix_today.py) puts heard-today last and re-scores trending, results in and taste, so after listening to a mix and coming back to the grid its lead story has changed: cover_tiles[0] is the new best and the heard one drops back or out. #mixList still holds the last render while loadMixes fetches; renderMixList replaces it in one frame. The READY tag (top tile, ready) appears once today's episode is written (the 05:00 edition, or a dormant mix opened, §359), and the headline line changes. To animate, tiles must be keyed (topic id or picture), not by position t0/t1/t2: render, read each key's old and new slot, and FLIP. Physical rule: a card never fades while in view and never passes through another, so in B the heard card dips and shrinks (moving 'behind'), its z-index swaps at the low point (scrub it so the swap lands unseen) and it settles into the back slot; the new lead rises straight into the top slot. A card leaving the three slides down behind the stack, clipped by the cover's overflow. The headline is text: cross-fade 150 ms, never moved. Staging: after the tab slide ends; several changed cards go 60 ms apart. Interrupt: a newer render re-FLIPs from the current transform. A photo cover shows the stack small in its corner: the same moves at that size. Tiles turn about their centres, as drawn today. Reduced motion: the new state at once.

options.tradeoff: Quiet and cheap; a picture fading inside a deck breaks the physical-card idea and hides that the order changed.

animations.title: A recommended topic joins the mix
animations.trigger: tap (+) on a recommended topic; tap Shuffle
animations.now: After the server answers the page is redrawn: the row is gone from the suggestions, a new row sits at the end of the list, and everything below jumps a row - in one frame.
animations.verdict: An item leaves toward where it went: add on the tap and move that one row up into the mix; Shuffle swaps the five rows with a quick staggered fade.
animations.notes: addRecTopic: saveMix PATCH {add:[id]}, then recState.shown drops the id and rerenderMixKeepScroll redraws #mixBody. The topic lands at the end of .mix-list (#mixOrder), right above the 'Recommended topics' heading - usually one or two rows above the row tapped, so the trip is short and vertical (one axis: straight, no arc). Optimistic: adding to your own mix almost never fails - draw the new state on the tap, send, and on refusal move it back with the message. B keeps one element for the whole trip (Replacements: never swap mid-move): FLIP the suggestion from its box to the new list row's box, already styled as a list row; its + becomes the play button only after landing (icon swap). Everything between - the heading, Shuffle, the other suggestions - moves by FLIP on the same 300 ms. If the end of the list is off screen (a long mix scrolled down), fall back to A. A uses the owner's §298 removal shape (exit, then the gap closes) plus the grid-rows expander for the new row. Shuffle, in every option: the five rows fade out 120 ms ease-in and the new ones fade up 6 px over 200 ms ease-out, 30 ms apart; instant under reduced motion. Note: an edit elsewhere (rename, visibility) re-runs openMix, which refetches the order and resets a shuffled set (bug list). Reduced motion: the new state at once.

animations.title: Dragging topics into a new order
animations.trigger: hold a topic's handle and drag
animations.now: Row follows the finger 1:1 with a shadow (one frame); others step aside on 140ms ease; on release every transform clears and the list redraws - the row jumps to its slot.
animations.verdict: The 1:1 drag is right. Add a lift on pick-up, 200 ms ease-in-out for neighbours, a settle from the finger on drop, a rubber band at the ends, and roll back a refused save.
animations.notes: startMixDrag adds .dragging (copper border, 0 8px 22px shadow, z 2, transition none) and .sorting in one frame; moveMixDrag sets the row's translateY to the finger's dy - unclamped, so the row can be carried far above or below the list - and moves each passed row ±pitch on a 140 ms ease transition (982). endMixDrag clears every transform and the class at once, then moveMixTopic redraws #mixBody in the new order: the row jumps from under the finger to its slot, and rows mid-transition snap. Skill: drags are direct (1:1, no easing) - kept; on release a spring takes over with the release velocity; at a bound, rubber-band after a dead zone (12 px; resistance 150; ceiling 64), never a free fly. Settle: after the redraw read the row's new top, set translateY(fingerTop - newTop), transition to 0 (FLIP). Lift: scale 1.02, and the shadow on a ::after whose opacity fades (never animate box-shadow). Neighbours are 'a reorder' in the timing table: 200-300 ms ease-in-out. Errors: the new order is drawn before saving and saveMix has no failed callback, so a refused save leaves the wrong order (bug) - FLIP back to the saved order with the message. Hit area: the handle is 22×34; give it 44×44. Keyboard: no way to reorder without a pointer (a Move up / Move down in a row menu). The owner chose this drag (10.5 packet #3); C keeps it closest. Reduced motion: .sorting transitions today (no override); every option makes neighbours jump and the drop instant.

options.recipe: Interruptibility + rubber banding + FLIP; spring as CSS linear()
options.tradeoff: The full recipe: the most code (a FLIP after the redraw, a velocity-aware settle) for a rare action.
options.why: Each part answers what today's drag drops: what I am holding, where it will land, and that it landed.
options.reduced: No lift or glide; rows jump into place; drop instant.

animations.title: The Public / Private switch
animations.now: Nothing moves until the server answers; then openMix redraws the page, so the knob's 160 ms ease never runs: knob, lock and words snap.
animations.verdict: Toggle on the tap and slide the knob that is already there (a transition, so a second tap turns it round); swap the lock with the icon-swap recipe; roll back if refused.
animations.notes: The CSS is there - track background 160 ms ease, knob transform translateX(20px) 160 ms ease, off under reduced motion - but toggleMixVisibility waits for saveMix, then calls openMix, which pushes the mix page onto itself and replaces #mixBody: the transition's element is new, so nothing ever animates. (openMix also re-posts /open, refetches recommendations and resets Shuffle - bug list.) The brief's note that it animates left is out of date: it moves by transform (good). Also stale: the CSS comment says the switch means private; the code means public (on = Public, open lock). A switch is a toggle: an interruptible transition, 'moving in place' 200-300 ms, ease-in-out. The lock changes with state, so the icon-swap recipe: both icons in the knob, cross-fading through scale .3 and a 3 px blur. 'Public'/'Private' and the sub-line sit in one grid cell and cross-fade (no width change). Optimistic: visibility almost never fails; on refusal slide back and say why. The hero line '· public' updates in place. The whole row is the target (good). B's shackle turns about its right foot (transform-origin 100% 100%). Reduced motion: the knob jumps; icons and words swap at once.

animations.title: Create: the folder becomes your mix
animations.trigger: tap Create (or Return) on New mix
animations.now: Create disables and waits with no sign of work; then the mix page pushes in from the right (320 ms) over the naming screen; the folder you named is left behind.
animations.verdict: A first success: the folder you just named should become the mix's cover in place, as the player grows from its picture; Create gets the async-button pending state.
animations.notes: confirmNewMix disables #nmCreate, POSTs /api/mixes, then openMix → navigate('mixdetail') → the owner's push (320 ms). Nothing shows during the POST (async-button recipe: spinner only after 300 ms, held 500 ms). Making a mix is a rare first success (Peak-end; the 'rarely' branch allows up to 500 ms a move). The naming screen's folder (.nm-folder, 128×128, paper, the folder icon or the chosen cover, the typed name inside) and the new page's hero art (.mix-hero-art, 84×84, top left of #mixBody) are one object to the listener. Precedent: the owner's player-open replaces the push with a grow from the tapped picture plus a 240 ms fade of the screen (§292); A does the same here, so it extends the push rule rather than breaking it - but it is the owner's call, which is why C keeps the push. Build with transforms only: an inert copy of .nm-folder, translate + scale(.66), transform-origin 0 0 - not Motion.ghost's left/top/width/height. Hide the real hero art until the copy lands, then hand over with a 120 ms fade, as the player does. The move is mostly horizontal (~110 px) with a small vertical change; if both axes pass 40 px on some phone, add a 10% arc. Interrupt: the new page is active from frame 1; Back finishes the flight at once (Motion.settle). Failure: a duplicate name is caught before the POST; a refusal re-enables Create and keeps the typed name. Reduced motion: the page swaps (today's 120 ms crossfade, or instant per the skill).

The round (+) in search results gets the icon swap only (the list is dense). Update the button in place: a re-render kills a running swap. animations.notes: toggleFollowCategory: guarded by catFollowBusy, POSTs the whole list to /api/categories/mine, GETs /api/categories, then renderCategoryChips and drawCategoryPanel - the button changes after two round trips. For following a person the owner picked (§298): 'The button changes on the tap: a tick draws in and it takes its new width (260 ms)' - Motion.follow. Reuse the behaviour (optimistic, the tick by stroke-dashoffset, rollback on refusal) but not the width animation (Properties: Motion.follow animates width): give .cat-follow a min-width that fits the tick and 'Following', so the label swaps in place. The star on the chip (and on the category's row in the Categories home) appears on the tap. B adds a rare secondary action linking cause and effect: the star travels to the chip; skip it when the chip is scrolled out of the row. Keep catFollowBusy (one write at a time) and the bottom line. Reduced motion: flips at once.

options.tradeoff: Small; the star on the chip still just appears.
options.why: It is the owner's own Follow motion minus the one property the skill forbids, and it answers on the tap.

Loop 2600.

animations.title: The morning dot on the myFAM tab
animations.trigger: the morning edition writes a mix; opening the tab clears it
animations.now: The copper dot appears and disappears in one frame (hidden toggles), while the unread count beside it pops in and shrinks away (§298).
animations.verdict: Same family as the unread count the owner picked: pop it in and shrink it away. Once a morning, so a single ring may earn its place.
animations.notes: checkFreshMixes (at launch, on return, every 15 minutes) fills freshMixes; drawMixDot toggles hidden on every [data-mix-dot] (one per tab bar copy). openPlayFAM → clearMixDot on the tab tap, the same moment as the tab slide. The Messages count uses Motion.badge (§298: pops in, bumps when it rises, shrinks away as an inert copy) - the dot is the same kind of thing (Similarity) drawn by another path. Reuse Motion.badge for the dot; only the visible tab bar animates (Motion.badge checks the active screen) - but on the tab tap the visible bar is the arriving screen's, which Motion.badge skips (:not(.arriving)), so the exit needs that check relaxed for the tab bar. Motion.badge pops from scale(0) with a 1.25 overshoot - the lead may tune that shared curve; the options say what the dot does whichever curve wins, and A's numbers are the skill's. B's ring is a secondary action on a rare event (once a morning), 450 ms, once - never a loop, since people aim at the tab. 'New today' on the card (.mix-a-new) stays still: it is information, and the card's own arrival carries it. Dot and ring scale from their centres. Reduced motion: the dot is simply there or gone.

options.name: Pop like a count
options.summary: The dot pops onto the tab the way unread counts do, and shrinks away when you open myFAM.
options.recipe: The owner's badge pop (§298); exits on an inert copy

options.why: The owner already chose how a tab badge arrives and leaves; the dot is the same object and should not snap.
options.reduced: Dot appears and goes at once.

animations.title: Finishing today's mix
animations.trigger: the last episode of a mix ends
animations.now: A text card ('You have finished listening to your Morning playlist for today') lifts in with the shared modal fade-and-lift (200 ms, 14 px).
animations.verdict: The end of the myFAM flow (Peak-end). A daily finish is routine: a quiet confirmation that shows what was done - today's cards stacked away - not a celebration.
animations.notes: finishMix clears mixPlay, hides the mini bar and adds .active to #mixDoneOverlay (a .modal-overlay holding a .nextup-card); the lift itself is shared (the lead's). The card has words only. Peak-end: people judge a flow by its end; the skill keeps celebration for real milestones and gives routine completions a quiet confirmation - a mix finishing is daily, so no sparks in A or B. 'Finished things recede: collapse, fade back or stack away' - the day's cards squaring into one stack says 'done' without words, in the mix's own look (the stacked deck, §616). Build: draw the mix's three cover_tiles fanned on the card as on its myFAM card (read from mixes by mixPlay.id before it is cleared), square them once the modal has landed (Staging: chain after the ~200 ms lift), then draw a copper check. If the queue has more, finishMix plays on and no card shows - unchanged. Reduced motion: the stack is drawn squared, with the check.

options.name: Deck squares up
options.summary: Today's three pictures sit fanned on the card; once it lands they square into a stack and a copper check draws on it.
options.spec: @260ms rotate ±7°→0, translate→0, 300ms (.77,0,.175,1) · check dashoffset 220ms (.32,.72,0,1) @560
options.tradeoff: Quiet and on-brand; the mix's pictures must be kept until the card is drawn.
options.why: It ends the flow on what was done, in the deck's own language, without turning a daily routine into a party.
options.reduced: Stack drawn squared, with the check.
options.demoText: Player dimmed behind; the card lifts in 300-500 (shared): three fanned pictures (Nvidia, AI, The Fed) on Morning's purple, 'You have finished listening to your Morning playlist for today', 'Fresh episodes on the same topics tomorrow', 'Back to myFAM'. 560-860 the fan squares into one stack; 860-1080 a copper check draws on the top card. Hold to 2400; loop.

options.name: Cards file in
options.summary: The day's cards, each marked Played, slide in from the right one after another onto the stack, then the check.
options.spec: ≤6 cards 260ms (.32,.72,0,1), 40ms apart · stack squares 300ms · check 220ms
options.tradeoff: Counts what was heard; longer (about 900 ms) for a routine end, and busier than the moment needs.
options.reduced: Stack drawn with the check.
options.demoText: Same card, an empty deck spot. 560: five small cards marked 'Played' slide in from the right onto the spot at 560/600/640/680/720, 260ms each; 980-1280 they square into one stack; 1280-1500 the check draws. Loop 2800.

options.tradeoff: Already says what happened; nothing ties the end to the mix the listener built.
options.reduced: Card appears at once.
options.demoText: Player dimmed behind; 300-500 the text card lifts in: 'You have finished listening to your Morning playlist for today', the sub line, 'Back to myFAM'. Hold to 2000; loop.
